questions.title: The Polished Pit Stop Car Wash — Revenue, Ratios, Averages and Inflation

subQuestions.questionText: John owns The Polished Pit Stop car wash. A basic wash is priced at R150 per wash. If 60 basic washes are completed in one day, calculate the total revenue for that day.
subQuestions.memoText:
Revenue = R150 × 60 = R9 000

Mark 1: multiplying R150 by 60
Mark 2: answer R9 000

subQuestions.questionText: Customers receive a 10% discount on Mondays. If the regular price for a basic car wash is R150, calculate the discounted amount they would pay.
subQuestions.memoText:
Discount = 10% × R150 = R15
Discounted price = R150 − R15 = R135
OR R150 × 0,9 = R135

Mark 1: calculating the 10% decrease
Mark 2: answer R135

subQuestions.questionText: Over the past month The Polished Pit Stop washed a total of 1 200 cars. The business operated for 30 days over the month. If the same number of cars were washed each day, calculate how many cars were washed per day.
subQuestions.memoText:
Cars per day = 1 200 ÷ 30 = 40 cars per day

Mark 1: dividing 1 200 by 30
Mark 2: answer 40 cars per day

subQuestions.questionText: Out of the 1 200 cars washed in the month, 700 were basic washes, 400 were premium washes and 100 were deluxe washes. Write, in simplest form, the ratio of basic washes to premium washes to deluxe washes.
subQuestions.memoText:
700 : 400 : 100
Divide each part by 100
= 7 : 4 : 1

Mark 1: writing the ratio 700 : 400 : 100
Mark 2: simplified ratio 7 : 4 : 1

subQuestions.questionText: Underline the correct word so that the definition reads true: The (median / mean) is calculated by finding the average of the two middle values in an even set of data that is ordered.
subQuestions.memoText:
median

(For an ordered data set with an even number of values, the median is the average of the two middle values.)

subQuestions.questionText: Underline the correct word so that the definition reads true: The (median / range) is a measure of spread.
subQuestions.memoText:
range

(The range = maximum − minimum, and is a measure of spread/dispersion. The median is a measure of central tendency.)

subQuestions.questionText: The car wash operates for 8 hours a day. The Polished Pit Stop washes 7 cars per hour on average. How many cars are washed in a day?
subQuestions.memoText:
8 hours × 7 cars per hour = 56 cars
Correct option: A (56)

Mark 1: multiplying 8 by 7
Mark 2: identifying option A (56)

subQuestions.questionText: Each car pays R150 for a basic car wash. Using your answer to Question 1.5.1 (56 cars per day), calculate the total income earned for basic washes in one day.
subQuestions.memoText:
Income = 56 × R150 = R8 400

Mark 1: multiplying 56 by R150
Mark 2: answer R8 400

subQuestions.questionText: The Polished Pit Stop uses detergent that costs R500 per 10-litre bottle, and 0,5 litres are used per car wash. Determine how many cars can be washed with one 10-litre bottle of detergent.
subQuestions.memoText:
Cars per bottle = 10 ÷ 0,5 = 20 cars

Mark 1: dividing 10 by 0,5
Mark 2: answer 20 cars

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the cost of detergent per car washed. (A 10-litre bottle costs R500 and washes 20 cars.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Cost per car = R500 ÷ 20 = R25

Mark 1: dividing R500 by 20
Mark 2: answer R25

subQuestions.questionText: The total operating costs for The Polished Pit Stop (labour, materials and other overheads) amount to R12 000 per month. If the business generates R33 600 in revenue each month, calculate its monthly profit.
subQuestions.memoText:
Profit = Income − Expenses
= R33 600 − R12 000
= R21 600

Mark 1: subtracting expenses from income
Mark 2: answer R21 600

subQuestions.questionText: The South African car wash market is predicted to reach $1 684,7 million by 2030. Write the value of $1 684,7 million in words, without using numerals.
subQuestions.memoText:
$1 684,7 million = $1 684 700 000

One billion, six hundred and eighty-four million, seven hundred thousand (dollars)

Mark 1: one billion
Mark 2: six hundred and eighty-four million, seven hundred thousand

subQuestions.questionText: The market is predicted to grow at an estimated annual inflation rate of 7,8%. Convert 7,8% to a decimal.
subQuestions.memoText:
7,8% = 7,8 ÷ 100 = 0,078

Mark 1: dividing by 100
Mark 2: answer 0,078

subQuestions.questionText:
The market is expected to grow at an inflation rate of 7,8% from 2023 to 2025. Complete the table to determine the missing values A to C for total revenue.

Row 1 — Revenue in 2023: R995 425 200 | Percentage value increase in 2024: R77 643 165,60 | Total revenue in 2024: (A)
Row 2 — Revenue in 2024: (A) | Percentage value increase in 2025: (B) | Total revenue in 2025: (C)
The method used to calculate the inflation rate (where each year's growth is applied to the new, larger value) is most similar to which of the following?
subQuestions.memoText:
B — Compound Interest

(The increase each year is calculated on the growing balance, not on the original amount, which is compound growth.)

questions.title: Michael Alberts' Salary Slip — Income Tax, UIF and Deductions

subQuestions.questionText: Michael's salary slip shows EMPLOYEE NAME: Mr Michael Alberts. Write down Michael's surname.
subQuestions.memoText:
Alberts

[Award 2 marks for the correct surname]

subQuestions.questionText: Michael's ID number is 8007115566778 and the payment date on the salary slip is 25-06-2025. Determine Michael's age in years as of the date shown on the salary slip.
subQuestions.memoText:
From the ID number, date of birth = 11 July 1980.
Payment date = June 2025, so his birthday for 2025 has not yet happened.
Age = 2025 − 1980 − 1 = 44 years old

Mark 1: reading year of birth 1980 from the ID number
Mark 2: 2025 − 1980
Mark 3: subtracting 1 (birthday not yet reached) → 44 years

subQuestions.questionText: Michael's monthly salary is R41 435,90 and his Old Mutual Pension deduction is R12 430,77. The maximum allowable pension fund deduction for tax is 27,5% of gross income. Use calculations to verify that Michael's annual taxable income amounts to R360 492,36 (rounded to two decimal places).
subQuestions.memoText:
Allowable pension deduction = 27,5% × R41 435,90 = R11 394,87
R11 394,87 < R12 430,77, so the capped amount R11 394,87 is used.
Monthly taxable income = R41 435,90 − R11 394,87 = R30 041,03
Annual taxable income = R30 041,03 × 12 = R360 492,36 ✓

Mark 1: 27,5% of gross
Mark 2: R11 394,87
Mark 3: comparing to actual pension / choosing R11 394,87
Mark 4: gross − pension
Mark 5: R30 041,03
Mark 6: × 12 → R360 492,36 (accept R360 492,33 with no rounding in steps)

subQuestions.questionText: The tax table brackets are: Bracket 1: R1 – R237 100; Bracket 2: R237 101 – R370 500; Bracket 3: R370 501 – R512 800; and so on. State the tax bracket that will be used to calculate Michael's tax payable on an annual taxable income of R360 492,36.
subQuestions.memoText:
Bracket 2 (R237 101 – R370 500)

[Award 2 marks for correctly identifying the 2nd tax bracket]

subQuestions.questionText: The medical tax credit is R364 per month for the principal member and R728 per month for the principal member and one dependant. Michael has one adult dependant. Determine Michael's annual total medical tax credit for himself and his spouse.
subQuestions.memoText:
Monthly credit (principal member + one dependant) = R728
Annual credit = R728 × 12 = R8 736

Mark 1: identifying R728 as the monthly credit
Mark 2: multiplying by 12
Mark 3: answer R8 736

subQuestions.questionText: Bracket 2 tax is calculated as R42 678 + 26% of taxable income above R237 100. The primary rebate is R17 235 per year. Michael's annual medical tax credit is R8 736. Determine the missing value A, Michael's monthly income tax contribution, using an annual taxable income of R360 492,36.
subQuestions.memoText:
Annual tax before rebates = R42 678 + 0,26 × (R360 492,36 − R237 100)
= R42 678 + 0,26 × R123 392,36
= R42 678 + R32 082,01
= R74 760,01
Less primary rebate and medical tax credit:
R74 760,01 − R17 235 − R8 736 = R48 789,01
Monthly tax A = R48 789,01 ÷ 12 = R4 065,75
(Accept R4 065,83 depending on rounding.)

Mark 1: taxable income above R237 100
Mark 2: 26% of that amount
Mark 3: adding R42 678
Mark 4: subtracting the rebate
Mark 5: subtracting the medical tax credit
Mark 6: dividing by 12 → A ≈ R4 065,75

subQuestions.questionText: A UIF contribution of 1% of salary is deducted monthly, with a maximum deduction of R177,12. Michael's UIF deduction on the slip is R177,12. Use calculations to determine whether his current UIF contribution equals 1% of his gross monthly income of R41 435,90.
subQuestions.memoText:
1% × R41 435,90 = R414,36
Michael's actual UIF deduction = R177,12
R177,12 ÷ R41 435,90 × 100 = 0,43%
R177,12 ≠ R414,36, so his contribution does NOT equal 1% of his gross salary — it is less, because the UIF deduction is capped at R177,12.

Mark 1: 1% × R41 435,90 = R414,36
Mark 2: comparing R177,12 to R414,36 (or calculating 0,43%)
Mark 3: correct conclusion (not equal / capped)

subQuestions.questionText: The salary slip shows TOTAL EARNINGS: R41 435,90 and TOTAL DEDUCTIONS: R18 680,63. Calculate the missing value C, Michael's net income.
subQuestions.memoText:
Net income C = Total earnings − Total deductions
= R41 435,90 − R18 680,63
= R22 755,27

(Accept answers around R22 517 – R22 518 if the candidate recalculates total deductions using their own tax value from 2.6.)

Mark 1: subtracting total deductions from total earnings
Mark 2: answer R22 755,27

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the term Tax Threshold.
subQuestions.memoText:
The tax threshold is the maximum amount of annual income a person can earn before they are required to start paying income tax.

[Award 2 marks for a correct definition]

questions.title: Top-Earning YouTubers — Averages, Quartiles, Outliers and Graphs

subQuestions.questionText: The net worth (in $ millions) of the Top-10 YouTubers is: 500; 200; 150; 104; 100; 100; 100; 80; 50; 45. Identify the modal net worth amount.
subQuestions.memoText:
$100 000 000 (i.e. $100 million)

(It appears three times, more often than any other value.)

[Award 2 marks for $100 million]

subQuestions.questionText: An outlier can be identified using: Outlier fence = Upper quartile + 1,5 × IQR. If this fence is less than the maximum value in the data set, the maximum value is an outlier. The ordered data (in $ millions) is: 45; 50; 80; 100; 100; 100; 104; 150; 200; 500. Show, with calculations, whether MrBeast's net worth ($500 million) is an outlier.
subQuestions.memoText:
Lower quartile Q1 = $80 million
Upper quartile Q3 = $150 million
IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 150 − 80 = $70 million
Outlier fence = Q3 + 1,5 × IQR = 150 + 1,5 × 70 = 150 + 105 = $255 million
$500 million > $255 million
Therefore MrBeast's net worth IS an outlier.

Mark 1: identifying Q1 = $80 million
Mark 2: identifying Q3 = $150 million
Mark 3: Q3 − Q1
Mark 4: IQR = $70 million
Mark 5: 150 + 1,5 × 70 = $255 million
Mark 6: conclusion — $500 million is an outlier

subQuestions.label: 3.1.3 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: A bar graph shows the Top-10 YouTubers, plotting each YouTuber's position (1 to 10) against their net worth. One bar has been omitted. Give suitable labels for the horizontal and vertical axes.
subQuestions.memoText:
Horizontal axis: Position of the Top-10 YouTubers (1 to 10)
Vertical axis: Net worth (in millions of dollars)

Mark 1–2: horizontal axis label
Mark 3–4: vertical axis label (including the unit, $ millions)

subQuestions.label: 3.1.3 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Complete the bar graph by drawing in the missing bar. The missing bar is for position 4 (Jeffree Star), whose net worth is $200 million. Describe the bar you would draw.
subQuestions.memoText:
A bar drawn at position 4, the same width as the other bars, reaching up to 200 on the vertical (net worth) axis.

Mark 1: bar in the correct position and width
Mark 2: bar drawn to a height of 200

subQuestions.label: 3.1.3 (c)
subQuestions.questionText:
Underline the correct option in each bracket to make the statements true:
(1) A bar graph is a way to visually represent (categorical / numerical) data.
(2) A (pie chart / histogram) can also be used to illustrate the above data set.
(3) The bar graph above is an example of a (vertical / horizontal) bar graph.
subQuestions.memoText:
(1) categorical
(2) pie chart
(3) vertical

Mark 1: categorical
Mark 2: pie chart
Mark 3: vertical

subQuestions.label: 3.1.3 (d)
subQuestions.questionText: On a pie chart of the Top-10 YouTubers' net worth, an angle has been drawn to represent MrBeast's net worth. The total net worth of all Top-10 YouTubers is $1 429 million and MrBeast's is $500 million. With calculations, show that the angle drawn (126°) is correct.
subQuestions.memoText:
Angle = (500 ÷ 1 429) × 360°
= 0,3499… × 360°
= 125,96°
≈ 126°
Therefore the angle drawn is correct.

Mark 1: 500 ÷ 1 429
Mark 2: × 360°
Mark 3: 125,96° (≈ 126°)
Mark 4: conclusion

subQuestions.label: 3.1.3 (e)
subQuestions.questionText: Calculate, to two decimal places, MrBeast's net worth ($500 million) as a percentage of the total net worth of the Top-10 YouTubers ($1 429 million).
subQuestions.memoText:
Percentage = 500 ÷ 1 429 × 100
= 34,9895…
= 34,99%

Mark 1: 500 ÷ 1 429 × 100
Mark 2: 34,99% (rounded to two decimal places)

subQuestions.questionText: A graph titled 'How content creators make their money' shows the income earned by content creators on social media, split into several revenue streams stacked on top of each other for 2023 and for 2024. Name the type of graph shown.
subQuestions.memoText:
A compound (stacked) bar graph.

(Also accept: dual bar graph / multiple bar graph.)

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The 2023 bar of the graph is made up of the following revenue streams (in dollars): $7,0 billion; $2,9 billion; $894 million; $341 million; $212 million; $118 million; $298 million. Show that content creators earned a total income of $11 763 000 000 in 2023.

It is stated that there was an increase of 16% in sponsorship income from 2023 to 2024. Sponsorship income was $7,0 billion in 2023 and $8,1 billion in 2024. Verify, with calculation, whether this statement is valid.
subQuestions.memoText:
Percentage increase = (8,1 − 7,0) ÷ 7,0 × 100
= 1,1 ÷ 7,0 × 100
= 15,71%
≈ 15,7%
This is not exactly 16%, therefore the statement is not valid (the actual increase is about 15,7%).

Mark 1: 8,1 − 7,0
Mark 2: difference = 1,1
Mark 3: ÷ 7,0
Mark 4: × 100 → 15,7%
Mark 5: conclusion — statement is incorrect

questions.title: Plastic Bags — Rates of Change, Decomposition and a Till Slip

subQuestions.questionText: In 2003 the cost of a plastic bag was set at 20 cents. The current rate is R1,20 per bag. Determine how many times more consumers are currently paying for plastic bags compared to the cost in 2003.
subQuestions.memoText:
20 cents = R0,20
R1,20 ÷ R0,20 = 6 times

Mark 1: converting 20 cents to R0,20
Mark 2: dividing R1,20 by R0,20
Mark 3: answer 6 times

subQuestions.questionText: An infographic shows the estimated minimum and maximum time (in years) it takes for different waste types to decompose in a landfill. Identify the product that takes the longest time to decompose, in terms of years.
subQuestions.memoText:
Styrofoam

[Award 2 marks — Styrofoam has the longest maximum decomposition time on the infographic]

subQuestions.questionText: Plastic bags take approximately 450 years to decompose in a landfill, whereas biodegradable bags decompose in about 6 months. Determine the percentage rate of change in decomposition time between the two types of bags, rounded to one decimal place. Use: Percentage change = (Difference in years ÷ Years for non-biodegradable bags) × 100.

A study suggests that plastic decomposes 10% faster in the ocean than on land. If it typically takes 450 years for plastic to decompose on land, calculate the time (in years) it would take for plastic to decompose in the ocean.
subQuestions.memoText:
10% of 450 = 45 years
Ocean time = 450 − 45 = 405 years
OR 450 × 0,9 = 405 years

Mark 1: 10% of 450
Mark 2: percentage decrease (450 − 45)
Mark 3: answer 405 years

subQuestions.questionText: In 2013 the Shoprite Group introduced recycled plastic bags. Determine how many plastic bags have been sold from 2013 to 2025 if 700 million plastic bags have been sold per year. Give your answer using the word 'billion'.
subQuestions.memoText:
From 2013 to 2025 is 13 years.
Total = 700 000 000 × 13 = 9 100 000 000
= 9,1 billion bags

Mark 1: 13 years
Mark 2: 700 000 000 × 13
Mark 3: 9 100 000 000 = 9,1 billion

subQuestions.questionText: In 2024 the group prevented 7 000 tonnes of plastic from reaching landfills. If this trend continues, determine how many tonnes of plastic will not find their way into landfills in the next 20 years.
subQuestions.memoText:
7 000 tonnes × 20 years = 140 000 tonnes

Mark 1: multiplying 7 000 by 20
Mark 2: answer 140 000 tonnes

subQuestions.label: 4.3.3 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: The 'planet' bag sells for R3 each. Every time a customer re-uses the bag after the first purchase, they get 50c off their grocery purchase. Determine the number of times a 'planet' bag must be re-used to cover its cost.
subQuestions.memoText:
Number of re-uses = R3,00 ÷ R0,50 = 6 times

Mark 1: dividing R3,00 by R0,50
Mark 2: answer 6 times

subQuestions.label: 4.3.3 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: A customer buys a 'planet' bag (R3) on the first purchase of a two-week period, then buys R250 of groceries every day for the two weeks (14 days), re-using the bag each day after the first purchase (50c saving per re-use). Calculate the total cost of the groceries, together with the 'planet' bag savings, for the two-week period.
subQuestions.memoText:
Total groceries = R250 × 14 = R3 500
Cost including the bag = R3 500 + R3,00 = R3 503
Re-uses = 13 days (all days except the first purchase)
Total savings = 13 × R0,50 = R6,50
Final cost = R3 503 − R6,50 = R3 496,50

Mark 1: R250 × 14 = R3 500
Mark 2: adding the R3,00 bag → R3 503
Mark 3: 13 re-use days
Mark 4: 13 × R0,50 = R6,50 savings
Mark 5: R3 503 − R6,50 = R3 496,50

subQuestions.questionText: A Checkers Hyper document shows a list of items purchased, quantities and prices, a TOTAL of R247,29, an 'Electronic Payment' line, VAT amounts, the date and time, and a message 'Please keep your till slip as proof of purchase.' State the type of financial document shown.
subQuestions.memoText:
A till slip (cash register slip / cash sale receipt).

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Several items on the till slip are marked with an asterisk (*). Explain the meaning of the asterisk (*) in this context.
subQuestions.memoText:
The asterisk indicates items that are VAT-exempt (zero-rated) — no VAT is charged on those items.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The till slip shows a TOTAL of R247,29, of which the VAT-exempt (0%) items total R62,97. The VAT-applicable (15%) portion is shown as R184,32. Show how the value of R184,32 was calculated.
subQuestions.memoText:
R184,32 = Total − VAT-exempt total
= R247,29 − R62,97
= R184,32

Mark 1: subtracting the VAT-exempt total from the overall total
Mark 2: answer R184,32

subQuestions.questionText: The R184,32 is the gross (VAT-inclusive) value of the 15%-rated items. Determine the missing value A, the total for the VAT-applicable items before VAT is added.
subQuestions.memoText:
A = R184,32 ÷ 1,15 = R160,28

Mark 1: dividing by 1,15
Mark 2: answer R160,28

questions.title: Ubuntu Threads — Break-Even Analysis, Probability and Box Plots

subQuestions.questionText: Naledi's business 'Ubuntu Threads' has a fixed expense of R5 000 per month, variable expenses of R120 per unprinted hoodie and an additional R50 for printing/design per hoodie. Give the equation Naledi will use to calculate her total expenses (E) in terms of the number of printed hoodies made (n).
subQuestions.memoText:
Variable cost per printed hoodie = R120 + R50 = R170
E = 5 000 + 170n

Mark 1: notation E = …
Mark 2: fixed cost + 5 000
Mark 3: combining the two variable costs (170)
Mark 4: the term 170n

subQuestions.questionText:
Income is calculated as I = 250 × number of hoodies. Using E = 5 000 + 170n, complete the table by filling in the shaded blocks.

Number of hoodies (n): 0 | 10 | 50 | 75 | 100
Expenses (E): ? | R6 700 | ? | ? | ?
Income (I): R0 | ? | R12 500 | R18 750 | R25 000
subQuestions.memoText:
Expenses (E), using E = 5 000 + 170n:
n = 0 → R5 000
n = 10 → R6 700 (given)
n = 50 → R13 500
n = 75 → R17 750
n = 100 → R22 000

Income (I), using I = 250n:
n = 0 → R0 (given)
n = 10 → R2 500
n = 50 → R12 500 (given)
n = 75 → R18 750 (given)
n = 100 → R25 000 (given)

Mark 1: Expenses at n = 0 and n = 100 (R5 000 and R22 000)
Mark 2: Expenses at n = 50 and n = 75 (R13 500 and R17 750)
Mark 3: Income at n = 10 (R2 500)

subQuestions.questionText: Use the table in Question 5.2 to draw two straight-line graphs on the grid provided — one showing the Expenses and one showing the Income for 'Ubuntu Threads' — for up to 100 hoodies. State the key features your graphs must show.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expenses line: straight line from (0; 5 000) to (100; 22 000).
Income line: straight line from (0; 0) to (100; 25 000).
Required features:
- suitable scale on the horizontal (number of hoodies) axis
- a key distinguishing the Expenses line from the Income line
- both lines plotted accurately using the table values
- dotted projection lines where used
- points (0; 0), (0; 5 000), (100; 25 000), (100; 22 000) correctly plotted
The lines cross at about n = 62 to 63 hoodies (the break-even point).

Mark 1: scale on the x-axis
Mark 2: key
Mark 3: dotted lines
Mark 4: point (0; 0)
Mark 5: point (0; 5 000)
Mark 6: point (100; 25 000)
Mark 7: point (100; 22 000)

subQuestions.questionText: From a sample of 150 hoodies sold by 'Ubuntu Threads', 60 were ordered without custom artwork. Naledi states that there is a 60% chance that a randomly selected hoodie will have custom artwork on it. Show, with calculations, whether this statement is correct.
subQuestions.memoText:
Hoodies with custom artwork = 150 − 60 = 90
P(custom artwork) = 90 ÷ 150 × 100 = 60%
Therefore the statement is correct.

Mark 1: 150 − 60 = 90
Mark 2: 90 ÷ 150 × 100
Mark 3: 60% and correct conclusion

subQuestions.questionText: Naledi tracks customer colour preferences: 50% prefer black, 0,3 prefer grey and 1/5 prefer navy blue. The same customers equally prefer either a custom design of an African mask or the African continent. A tree diagram of this information has shaded blocks to be completed. Write the missing probabilities as fractions: (i) the probability for black; (ii) the probability for grey; (iii) the probability for navy blue; (iv) the probability for each design choice.
subQuestions.memoText:
black = 50% = 1/2
grey = 0,3 = 3/10
navy blue = 1/5
each design (African mask / African continent) = 1/2 (equal preference)

Mark 1: black = 1/2
Mark 2: grey = 3/10
Mark 3: navy blue = 1/5 and design branches = 1/2

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the probability that a randomly selected customer will choose either a grey or a navy-blue hoodie. (Grey = 3/10, navy blue = 1/5.)
subQuestions.memoText:
P(grey or navy blue) = 3/10 + 1/5
= 3/10 + 2/10
= 5/10
= 1/2

Mark 1: adding the two probabilities
Mark 2: answer 1/2 (0,5)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the probability, as a decimal, that a customer does not prefer black hoodies. (Black = 1/2.)
subQuestions.memoText:
P(not black) = 1 − 1/2 = 1/2 = 0,5

Mark 1: subtracting from 1
Mark 2: answer 0,5

subQuestions.questionText: 'Ubuntu Threads' monthly sales data has the five-number summary: Minimum = R12 500; Lower Quartile = R14 000; Median = R15 000; Upper Quartile = R15 500; Maximum = R16 000. Describe how you would insert these five values on a number line (marks are given only if the number line is labelled with correct increment values).
subQuestions.memoText:
Draw a number line with a suitable constant scale, e.g. increments of R500 from R12 500 to R16 000.
Plot: R12 500 (minimum), R14 000 (lower quartile), R15 000 (median), R15 500 (upper quartile), R16 000 (maximum).

Mark 1: correct constant scale/increments on the number line
Mark 2: all five values plotted in the correct positions
